newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says budget deal has to be done this year.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says budget deal has to be done this year.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Wednesday there had to be an agreement with Congress to balance the U.S. budget this year, and it would be his first priority after he returns from a U.S.-Russian summit in Helsinki.

"Our first order of business when I get back from Helsinki must be to finish the job of balancing the budget. We have to do it this year," Clinton told reporters in the White House after meeting the leaders of congressional budget committees. The president was scheduled to leave for Helsinki later on Wednesday.

Clinton described his meeting with congressional budget committee leaders at the White House as "very productive," and said it gave new impetus to talks on balancing the budget. Both Democrats and Republicans have said they want to get rid of the deficit by 2002 but disagree on the means of getting there.

The president said it was agreed that during the congressional recess over the next two weeks there would be more meetings between White House officials and congressional budget committee leaders to try to "reduce the differences" on a variety of issues.
Then, after the recess, Clinton told reporters, he personally would meet with leaders of the House and Senate and "we will be able to make rapid progress" toward balancing the budget.
"We have circled these issues long enough," Clinton said. "It's time now to give the American people a balanced budget and I believe we will do it and do it this year."
